messages:
anne: hey, heads up — hit a weird role-derivation loop on canary after the roles schema refactor. observed CPU spike + repeated derivation calls and audit logs missing for those requests.
raj: which canary cluster?
anne: cluster-c-3, canary build v2026.03.16. quick curl to /v1/auth returned 500 during token resolve.
morgan: any stack / logs?
anne: paste from auth service: 
```
ERROR auth/derive: deriveRoles failed: kms: decrypt error: ciphertext malformed (key_id=projects/redwood/keys/roles-seal-v2)
WARN auth/derive: txn retry (attempt=4) while backfilling default_roles
ERROR auth: deriveRoles -> panic: role derivation loop detected: re-entrancy with same request_id
```
raj: hmm kms decrypt malformed — did we rotate the roles-seal key without adding the old KID alias?
dmitri: we deployed the schema change which added role_seal_v2 and switched the default seal to v2 in feature flag, but the KMS alias mapping task didn't run in canary due to IAM scoping. that explains malformed ciphertext on older seals.
lindsey: so backfill tried to decrypt old blobs, failed, retried, and the derivation code falls back to re-compute and calls itself? that's the loop?
anne: yes. code path: backfill -> decrypt seal -> if decrypt error -> attempt migration -> call deriveRoles (for safety) -> deriveRoles hits missing default role and enqueues another backfill call -> cycle.
morgan: noted. audit logs gone because the request fails before the audit hook writes the envelope. we should avoid retries that re-enter derivation.
raj: immediate mitigation options: 1) feature-flag rollback to v1 default seal, 2) patch deriveRoles to short-circuit on KMS decrypt errors, 3) stop the canary backfill worker.
dmitri: I started a canary backfill pause: `kubectl -n infra scale deployment backfill-worker --replicas=0` on cluster-c-3. paused at 2234567908.
deploy-bot: deploy: pause backfill-worker on cluster-c-3 was successful (user=dmitri, ts=2234567908).
lindsey: good. next: do we roll the default seal back to v1? that would let decrypt succeed and resume normal behavior, but we need to ensure v1 key still available in KMS.
raj: check KMS keys: `gcloud kms keys list --location global --keyring prod-keys | grep roles-seal` — if v1 exists, set alias and flip flag.
anne: quick check: v1 key exists but the service account used by canary nodes did not have kms.keys.get for the v1 key due to a scoping bug. fixable by IAM patch.
morgan: plan: 1) keep backfill paused, 2) add old KID alias into canary KMS mapping + grant kms.get to canary SA, 3) flip default seal back to v1 OR forward-unwrap existing seals by running a migration on a host with access.
dmitri: I'll open an infra PR to add iam:roles/kms.cryptoKeyDecrypter for canary nodes and request an urgent service-account grant.
lindsey: also we should patch deriveRoles to not re-enqueue backfill on decrypt errors — treat as fatal for that request and return a specific 5xx with audit hook still firing. small code change, low-risk.
raj: agree — conservative behavior now. anne, can you draft a short postmortem note and update the rollout checklist to require KMS alias verification + RBAC test before seal flips?
anne: on it. will also attach the logs and the `kubectl` command.
morgan: one more thing — add an automated check in CI that runs `kms:decrypt` against a fixture ciphertext with both v1 and v2 keys before we switch default.
raj: action items: dmitri -> IAM grant (ETA 30m), anne -> rollback checklist + PM (ETA 45m), morgan -> patch deriveRoles short-circuit PR (ETA 2h), lindsey -> monitor canary CPU + audit logs.
dmitri: starting IAM grant now.
anne: thanks. if anyone sees unexpected auth errors on other clusters ping here. :warning:
deploy-bot: canary rollback in-progress: featureflag roles_seal_default -> v1 (initiated user=dmitri, ts=2234567920).
